title: Crunchy Dumpling Lettuce Wraps
subtitle: Korean-inspired lettuce wraps with a Jain TVP filling, homemade gochujang, and crunchy dumpling strips.
protein: ~20g protein per adult serving — from TVP, plus peanuts in the chili crisp

method.title: Soak the TVP
items: Stir together hot water {2 cups}, soy sauce {1½ tbsp}, grated ginger {1 tsp}, hing {¼ tsp} and sugar {½ tsp} in a large bowl
Add the dry TVP {150g} and stir well
Cover and set aside for 15–20 minutes. It returns in Step 8 with all its liquid.

method.title: Make the Jain gochujang
items: In a small bowl, whisk gochugaru {3 tbsp — or 2 tbsp Kashmiri chili powder + 1 tbsp regular chili powder}, white miso {2 tbsp}, brown sugar {2 tbsp}, rice vinegar {1 tbsp} and salt {¼ tsp}
Add warm water {3 tbsp} a spoonful at a time, whisking, until it forms a thick glossy paste that falls slowly off the spoon
Let it rest 10 minutes so the chili flakes hydrate and the raw edge softens
Makes about ⅔ cup — you need 2 tbsp today, the rest keeps refrigerated for a month

method.title: Make the Jain chili crisp
items: Put gochugaru {2 tbsp}, sesame seeds {1 tbsp}, crushed peanuts {2 tbsp}, hing {¼ tsp}, sugar {½ tsp} and salt {½ tsp} into a heatproof bowl
Heat neutral oil {⅓ cup} with the julienned ginger {1 tbsp} in a small pan over medium heat, 4–5 minutes, until the ginger is pale gold and the bubbling slows
Take the pan off the heat, wait 30 seconds, then pour the oil {⅓ cup} and ginger {1 tbsp} over the bowl — it will sizzle hard for a few seconds
Stir and cool completely. Set aside — it goes on at serving, Step 10.

method.title: Mix the sauce, reserve the toddler's share
items: Whisk soy sauce {5 tbsp}, water {6 tbsp}, toasted sesame oil {2 tbsp}, brown sugar {2 tbsp} and cornstarch {1 tbsp} until completely smooth, no lumps
Scoop 3 tbsp of this plain sauce into a small bowl and set it aside — that's the toddler's, and it returns in her portion right after Step 8, before the gochujang goes in
Now stir the Jain gochujang {2 tbsp} into the sauce left in the big bowl. Set aside.

method.title: Prep everything else
items: Slice celery {2 stalks} thin on a sharp diagonal — you want long shards, not chunks
Shred the cabbage {~4 cups}, julienne the red bell pepper {1 medium}, grate the ginger {2 tbsp}

Julienne a small carrot and keep it in a separate bowl — toddler only. Microwave it with water {1 tbsp}, covered, 2 minutes until just tender; drain and set aside — it returns in her portion right after Step 8.
Stack the dumpling wrappers {14} and cut into strips about ½ cm wide
Separate, wash and thoroughly dry the butter lettuce {2 heads} into cups — wet leaves make the filling slide out

method.title: Crisp the dumpling strips
items: Air fryer (recommended): toss the strips with oil {1 tbsp} until barely slicked. Spread in a single layer in the Ninja Crispi and run 330°F for 4–6 minutes, shaking at the 3-minute mark. Pull them while still pale gold — they darken and crisp further as they cool.
Deep-fry alternative: heat oil {2 cups} in a heavy saucepan over high heat; fry the strips in batches, stirring gently, until golden. Lift onto a lined plate.
Set the finished strips aside — they get seasoned next, then go on at serving, Step 10

method.label: Toddler — pull her strips now, before seasoning
items: Take a small handful of the crisped strips out and put them on her plate
Salt them very lightly and leave them alone otherwise
Do this before the next step — white pepper is mild but there's no reason for her to have it

method.title: Season the adult strips
items: Toss the remaining strips with white pepper {¼ tsp}, mushroom powder {½ tsp}, sugar {¼ tsp} and salt {¼ tsp} while still warm

method.title: Cook the filling
items: Heat neutral oil {2 tbsp} in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat
Add hing {¼ tsp} and swirl for 10 seconds until it smells savory and nutty — don't let it brown
Add the celery {2 stalks} and grated ginger {2 tbsp}. Cook 2 minutes — the celery should stay squeaky, not go soft.
Add the shredded cabbage {~4 cups} and red bell pepper {1 medium}. Cook 5–7 minutes until the cabbage wilts and the pepper just softens.
Add the soaked TVP {150g} from Step 1 along with all its remaining liquid. Stir through and cook 2 minutes. Stop here — nothing spicy has gone in yet.

method.label: Toddler — pull her filling now, before the gochujang sauce
items: Scoop about 1 cup of the filling and TVP out of the pan into a small saucepan
Add the softened carrot from Step 5
Pour in the plain reserved sauce {3 tbsp} from Step 4
Simmer 2 minutes, stirring, until it thickens and coats everything
Finish off the heat with ghee {½ tsp}
Serve with her plain salted strips from earlier, and either torn butter lettuce or a small bowl of rice
Hing and ginger are already in this and both are fine for her — the only things she's missing are the gochujang and the chili crisp; everything else is identical to the adult version, carrot included

method.title: Finish the adult filling
items: Pour the gochujang sauce from Step 4 over what's left in the big pan
Cook 5–7 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is glossy and thick enough to sit in a lettuce leaf without running out the bottom
Taste and adjust salt — it should be sweet-salty first, heat second

method.title: Assemble
items: Spoon the filling into the butter lettuce cups from Step 5
Top each with the seasoned dumpling strips from Step 7, toasted sesame seeds {2 tbsp} and chopped celery leaves {¼ cup}
Finish with Jain chili crisp {to taste} from Step 3
Add the strips right at the table — they go soft within a couple of minutes of touching the sauce

method.label: What changed from the original
method.text: Onion → celery, sliced thin, plus hing bloomed in the oil. Garlic → hing. Green onion → celery leaves or coriander. Carrot → red bell pepper for adults (real carrot stays only in the toddler's portion). Bouillon cube → soy sauce + ginger + hing in the soaking water — cubes almost always carry onion or garlic powder. Gochujang and chili crisp are made from scratch here since most jarred brands, including Lao Gan Ma, list garlic. "Chicken spice" → white pepper, sugar, salt, mushroom powder. Wrappers: buy Chinese-style (flour, water, salt) — some gyoza wrappers contain egg, check the packet.

method.label: Appliance notes
method.text: Ninja Crispi for the strips: it runs hotter than most air fryers, 330°F is its floor and it's plenty here — start checking at 3 minutes, these go from pale to burnt in about 45 seconds. Wide sauté pan, not a wok, for the filling — you want the cabbage to wilt and lose water fast, a crowded pan steams it into mush. Small pan for the chili crisp — deep enough that ⅓ cup of oil is at least 2cm deep, or the ginger scorches before it crisps. Instant Pot isn't useful here — nothing benefits from pressure, and TVP just needs a soak.

method.label: Recipe notes
method.text: Celery is doing real work — slice it thin on a steep diagonal; cut into rounds it reads as "celery," cut into shards it reads as the sweet allium note the original wanted. Salt check: there's soy sauce in both the TVP soak and the sauce, so taste before adding extra salt at Step 9. The gochujang improves overnight — if you make it a day ahead, the miso rounds out and the chili loses its raw bite. No dumpling wrappers? Cut flour tortillas or spring roll pastry into strips instead — same treatment, slightly less shattery. Leftovers: filling keeps 3 days refrigerated and reheats well; store the strips and chili crisp separately at room temperature, never in the fridge. Heat level is moderate as written — halve the gochujang for a milder version, or serve it on the side and let people stir their own in.
